title: Sagas and compensating transactions

kcs.statement: A saga splits a distributed transaction into a sequence of local transactions, each paired with a compensating transaction that semantically undoes it if a later step fails.
In an orchestrated saga a central orchestrator tells each service what to do next; in a choreographed saga each service reacts to events from the previous step, with no central controller.
Unlike two-phase commit, a saga holds no locks across steps, so other requests can see intermediate states, and its steps and compensations must be idempotent because they may be retried.
